market_view: Calm regime: VIX 15.6, down 15% in five days; dollar firm near its 52-week high and 10-year yield near 4.5%. Crude has fallen 26% in 20 days, but new Iran and Strait of Hormuz headlines point to a fresh supply risk.

oil_gas.catalyst: 'Oil prices jump 5% after U.S. revokes Iran oil sanctions waiver following ship attacks' (NBC News) and 'Oil prices jump more than 4% after Trump threatens to bomb Iran and reimpose naval blockade' (CNBC), plus 'Exxon signals Q2 profit windfall' (Reuters). The 07-06 closes (WTI -0.2%, XOM -0.5%) do not yet show the jump, and a waiver revocation plus blockade threat is a policy escalation that can last weeks.
oil_gas.reasoning: A named supply shock after a 26% crude slide, with XOM still 20% off its high. XOM moves only 0.33-0.61 times crude and part of the jump will be in the open; geopolitical spikes often fade, so confidence stays just above the bar.

gold_miners.reasoning: Gold +1% yesterday but down 7.5% in 20 days; Morningstar says gold is in a bear market. The $9 bln tie-up commentary does not name NEM. Firm dollar and a jobs report inside the window add variance, not direction.

chips.reasoning: Only an NVIDIA blog post; the semi ETF +2% yesterday is priced in. NVDA is 17% off its high with no specific news; TSMC monthly sales around the 10th are a scheduled event without a one-sided setup.

pharma.reasoning: No LLY trial, approval or pricing news. LLY is 2.4% from its high after a 26% 60-day run; the sector fell 1.1% yesterday. Earnings season adds variance.

copper_uranium.reasoning: Headlines are a small uranium mine protest, a junior copper stake and a CCJ listicle; none reaches FCX. Copper +1% yesterday is priced in; FCX down 12% in 20 days with no named cause to reverse.

would_change_my_mind: Signs of Iran de-escalation or reinstated waivers (oil gives back the jump) would make oil flat; a guidance raise or supply outage for NEM, NVDA, LLY or FCX would justify a long there.

handoff.what_changed: Iran escalation: tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, the US revoked an Iran oil sanctions waiver, and Trump threatened bombing and a naval blockade; oil reportedly jumped 4-5% after the 07-06 close. Exxon signalled a Q2 profit windfall. Went long XOM on that supply-shock catalyst; the other four families stay flat.

oil_gas.why: Named supply shock (Iran waiver revoked, Hormuz tanker attacks, blockade threat) not yet in the 07-06 closes; confidence 0.53.

gold_miners.why: Gold in a bear market with a firm dollar; no NEM-specific catalyst.

chips.why: No NVDA-specific catalyst; sector bounce already priced in.

pharma.why: LLY near highs with no trial, approval or pricing news.

copper_uranium.why: No headline reaches FCX; copper move priced in.

open_storylines.name: Iran / Strait of Hormuz escalation
open_storylines.note: Watch for an actual blockade or strikes (supports the XOM long) versus de-escalation or waiver reinstatement (exit signal); check WTI and Brent closes.

open_storylines.name: Crude slump
open_storylines.note: WTI was down 26% in 20 days and back at pre-Iran-war levels on 07-06; the Iran news may reverse it. Watch OPEC+ and output growth.

open_storylines.name: Exxon Q2 windfall signal
open_storylines.note: Reuters says Exxon signalled a Q2 profit windfall; XOM Q2 earnings in late July fall inside or near the hold window and add variance.

open_storylines.name: Gold bear market
open_storylines.note: Morningstar cut near-term gold assumptions; a $9 bln gold-miner tie-up (not NEM) was reported. Watch the dollar, real rates, the jobs report and the NEM Q2 call.

open_storylines.name: Cigar Lake suspension
open_storylines.note: Watch the restart timeline and uranium spot; leader is FCX so impact is indirect. No update in this record.

open_storylines.name: Copper to aluminium substitution
open_storylines.note: Watch whether more automakers switch away from copper (demand headwind for FCX). No update in this record.

open_storylines.name: Q2 earnings season and Fed under Warsh
open_storylines.note: Earnings of XOM, NEM, LLY, FCX and NVDA peers in July-August and the jobs report raise variance; not a reason to be long.

handoff.next_job: On the next decision day, read this note, check whether the XOM long is still justified by the Iran/Hormuz storyline (exit to flat on clear de-escalation or once the 10-day horizon ends), then re-check all five families for a named catalyst in the new headlines.
